summary: OpenAI's GPT-5.4 Thinking card presents GPT-5.4 as a GPT-5-series reasoning model with stronger cyber capability and a larger cyber-safeguard stack than earlier general-purpose releases. The document treats it as High in Biological/Chemical and Cybersecurity capability, while keeping AI self-improvement below High and highlighting residual risks in prompt injection, long agent runs, and cyber misuse.

capabilities.text: GPT-5.4 Thinking is a reasoning model trained through reinforcement learning to deliberate before answering, improve its strategy, and better follow safety and task policies.
The model shows stronger workspace-state handling in long rollouts, including better preservation of simulated user work while undoing its own changes.
For computer-use settings, OpenAI trained it to follow both platform-level and developer-provided confirmation policies for high-risk actions.
OpenAI reports enough cyber capability across CTF, CVE-Bench, Cyber Range, and external testing to treat the model as Cyber High under its framework.
OpenAI reports that AI self-improvement evaluations remain below its High threshold, even though some software and ML benchmark results improve over comparison models.

evaluations.context: Difficult `not_unsafe` categories compared with GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2 Thinking.
Multi-turn adversarial simulations scored for policy-compliant responses.
Model-level resampling of GPT-5.2 Thinking-like traffic, excluding additional safety-stack layers.
Known connector and function-call attacks from training-data splits.
Rubric-graded health conversations with GPT-5.2 comparison.

evaluations.result: 0.86 avoidance; 0.18 perfect reversion; 0.53 user work preserved
evaluations.context: Agentic workspace safety evaluations for preserving user-produced changes.
CoT-Control suite; lower controllability is considered safer.
Fifteen emulated-network scenarios with pass/fail over 16 trials.

evaluations.result: 88% Network Attack Simulation; 73% Vulnerability Research and Exploitation; 48% Evasion; 11% CyScenarioBench average
evaluations.context: External cyberoffensive challenges with long-turn elicitation.
Policy-compliance evaluation for cyber prompts and generations.

safety_findings.text: OpenAI treats the model as High in Biological/Chemical and Cybersecurity capability, while saying the cyber call is precautionary because the model meets canary thresholds rather than proven real-world High behavior.
OpenAI reports challenging disallowed-content performance mostly near GPT-5.2 Thinking, including significant gains for illicit nonviolent behavior and self-harm.
Prompt-injection robustness improves for connector attacks and declines slightly for function-call attacks, with limited generalization evidence because both are training-data splits.
CoT monitorability is below GPT-5 Thinking in aggregate, but OpenAI argues key regressions in Memory and Anti-Scheming may reflect flaws in the evaluation labels and monitors.
Apollo Research reports low no-nudge deception, no observed covert subversion against developers, explicit-goal sandbagging, and a 0.56 mean sabotage score.
The cyber safeguard stack includes model safety training, online monitoring, account enforcement, Trusted Access for Cyber, and security controls around model assets.

limitations.text: The challenging content benchmarks are intentionally hard and not representative of routine production traffic.
The representative-prompt pilot is time-bound, model-layer-only, and subject to drift and reconstruction limits.
Prompt-injection results do not demonstrate robustness to novel attack families because the evaluated splits overlap the training setup.
HealthBench analysis identifies weaker context-seeking when the model lacks needed health information.
Preparedness testing is a lower bound because different scaffolds, fine-tuning, prompting, or longer rollouts could elicit stronger capability.
Cyber Range omits hardened targets and realistic defensive pressure, so it is necessary but not sufficient evidence for real campaign capability.
GPT-5.4 Thinking fails four Cyber Range scenarios and underperforms GPT-5.3-Codex on the suite overall.
OpenAI has not observed GPT-5.4-specific internal misalignment propensities, but says High cyber capability makes internal deployment posture more important.

practical_implications.text: Use GPT-5.4 for complex debugging, architecture, and multi-step code reasoning, but verify edits with tests and review.
Treat destructive shell commands, file deletions, resets, and cleanups as high-review actions even when the model appears confident.
Keep security tasks clearly authorized and defensive because the card treats the model as Cyber High.
Do not rely on prompt-injection scores as a complete defense; inspect untrusted tool output and issue content before acting on it.
Use explicit permissions and scoped workspaces for long agent runs so mistakes can be contained and reverted.

coverage_notes: The digest uses pages 4-33 of the GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card and excludes the GPT-5.4 mini appendix except for scope. Where extraction omitted chart values, the digest relies on text and tables with explicit numbers.
